hints: The 30° angle is measured from the horizontal, so identify the component opposite that angle.
walkthrough: The vertical component is opposite the 30° angle to the horizontal.
Its magnitude is 4.8 sin 30° = 2.4 N.
The component acts vertically downward because the string slopes downward from the beam to the ground.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses 4.8 sin 30° to obtain a vertical tension component of 2.4 N.

hints: Take moments about the hinge, so the unknown hinge force has no turning effect.
Use the downward 2.4 N component from part (a)(i) at 1.20 m from the hinge.
walkthrough: Take moments about the hinge. The 8.2 N spring force has an anticlockwise moment of 8.2 × 0.50 N m.
The beam weight, block weight and downward vertical tension component give clockwise moments W × 0.60, 0.30 × 0.80 and 2.4 × 1.20 N m respectively.
Solving gives 4.10 = 0.60W + 3.12, so W = 1.63 N, reported as 1.6 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms at least one correct moment about the hinge using the stated force and its perpendicular distance.
Solves the moment equation to obtain the beam weight as 1.6 N.

hints: Because the beam is in equilibrium, its horizontal forces must balance.
The string angle is to the horizontal, so its horizontal component is 4.8 cos 30° N.
walkthrough: The horizontal forces on the beam balance because the beam is in equilibrium.
The horizontal component of the string tension is 4.8 cos 30° = 4.16 N.
The hinge provides an equal horizontal component in the opposite direction, so its magnitude is 4.2 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses 4.8 cos 30° to obtain a horizontal hinge-force component of 4.2 N.

hints: For a spring that obeys Hooke’s law, use the elastic-energy expression involving force and compression.
Set 0.32 J equal to ½ × 8.2 N × x, then solve for x.
walkthrough: For the compressed spring, Eₚ = ½Fx.
Substitute the elastic potential energy and spring force: 0.32 = ½ × 8.2 × x.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses Eₚ = ½Fx for the spring.
Substitutes 0.32 J and 8.2 N to obtain a compression of 0.078 m.

hints: Use the block’s stated weight and its vertical drop from A to B.
The magnitude of the gravitational-potential-energy decrease is weight × height change.
walkthrough: For a vertical change, the magnitude of the gravitational-potential-energy change is mgΔh = WΔh.
The block has weight 0.30 N and falls through 0.090 m from A to B.
The decrease is 0.30 × 0.090 = 0.027 J.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses ΔEₚ = mgΔh or the equivalent relation ΔEₚ = WΔh.
Uses 0.30 N and 0.090 m to calculate a decrease of 0.027 J.

hints: With air resistance negligible, the loss of gravitational potential energy becomes an increase in kinetic energy.
Use the 0.027 J loss from part (c)(i) and the 0.044 J kinetic energy at B to find the kinetic energy at A.
The stated 0.30 N weight gives the block mass through m = W / g before applying Eₖ = ½mv².
walkthrough: The block loses 0.027 J of gravitational potential energy from A to B, so its kinetic energy increases by 0.027 J.
At B the kinetic energy is 0.044 J, so at A it is 0.044 − 0.027 = 0.017 J.
The block mass is m = W / g = 0.30 / 9.81 = 0.0306 kg.
Use Eₖ = ½mv²: 0.017 = ½(0.30 / 9.81)v², giving v² = 1.11 m² s⁻² and v = 1.1 m s⁻¹.
Alternatively, calculate the speed at B from 0.044 = ½(0.30 / 9.81)v_B², then use v_B² = v_A² + 2(9.81)(0.090) to obtain the same speed at A.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses Eₖ = ½mv² to relate a kinetic energy to the block’s speed.
Either uses energy conservation to obtain 0.017 J kinetic energy at A, or finds the speed at B and applies v_B² = v_A² + 2g(0.090).
Obtains the speed at A as 1.1 m s⁻¹.

hints: Consider the force and acceleration separately in the horizontal and vertical directions.
With air resistance negligible, the block’s weight is the only force and it acts vertically.
walkthrough: Air resistance is negligible, so the only force on the block is its weight.
Weight acts vertically downward, so there is no horizontal resultant force.
Therefore the horizontal acceleration is zero and the horizontal component of velocity remains constant.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the weight or resultant force is vertical, so there is no horizontal force.

hints: At A the block is already descending, so the magnitude of its vertical velocity is not zero.
Gravity gives a constant downward acceleration, so the magnitude of the downward vertical velocity increases uniformly.
walkthrough: At A, the block is travelling downward and therefore has a non-zero vertical-velocity magnitude.
With negligible air resistance, gravity provides constant vertical acceleration throughout the movement to B.
The magnitude vY therefore increases at a constant rate, so draw a straight line with positive gradient from a non-zero value at tA to tB.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a straight line with positive gradient from a non-zero vY value at tA to tB.
